description.value:
After the B2 Wingman’s commercial flop in the mid 2010s, Militech had no plans for a third. Yet, after decades of requests for a ‘reprisal,’ they announced the B3 in the 2040s. To put it bluntly, the B3 was a hastily put together sequel, made to capitalize on niche fan nostalgia while minimizing production costs, and thus flopped harder than its predecessor. Yet, on paper, the B3 is a remarkable sidearm — relatively low cost, hefty firepower, and reliable, though lacking in precision. Interestingly, these are the exact reasons why some special forces operators prefer it, as with enough skill and maneuverability this forgotten relic can be quite the powerful reminder of how good a piece of abandonware can really be.

Cost: 500eb (Expensive)

Class: Very Heavy Pistol • Skill: Handgun • Range: Pistol

Damage: 4d6 • Capacity: 6 • ROF: 2 • Hands: 1

Alt. Firing Modes: None

Concealable: No

Slots: 2 • Attachments: Laser Sight • Mods: None

Special Features: Incompatible with Capacity modifying Attachments and Pistol Auto Sear. All Attacks with this weapon suffer a -2 penalty to their Attack Check. When firing at a target beyond 6m/yds, this weapon deals 1d6 less damage (3d6). The Laser Sight can be activated or deactivated as an Action. While it is active and wielding this weapon in two hands, it functions as Excellent Quality but incurs a -2 penalty to Stealth Checks, or a -4 against characters utilizing Infrared/Nightvision [Laser Sight]. Requires BODY 6+ or a Cyberarm to wield unless Mounted.

Range: Pistol
Pre-installed: Laser Sight (effects already included in these stats)

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Weapons > Weapon Catalog).
